title: Finite integral scalar extension of the specified isomorphism compact-support exchange
statement:
Fix the finite-field and small pro-etale conventions of [def-pur-conventions], so $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ has characteristic $p$, and fix $\ell\ne p$ and finite extensions $E\subset F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings and uniformizers [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $h=e(F/E)\ge1$, defined by $(\varpi_E)\mathcal O_F=(\varpi_F^h)$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and let $g:Y'\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ be an isomorphism of underlying schemes, with Cartesian pullback $f':X'\to Y'$ and $g':X'\xrightarrow{\sim}X$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. No $k$-linearity of $g,g'$ is assumed. Choose a compactification $f=pj$ and its isomorphism base change $f'=p'j'$, with induced $\bar g$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements].

For $D=E,F$ use completed coefficient sheaves $R_{D,T}=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{D,T}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and the derived-complete constructible finite-Tor categories $D^b_{ctf}(T,\mathcal O_D)$ with uniform reduction intervals [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Write $P_{f,D}=Rf_{!,D}$, $P_{f',D}=Rf'_{!,D}$ for the separately derived proper/open compact-support functors [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Let $G_{u,D}=Lu^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$ for $u=g,g',\bar g$, and let
$$\xi_{D,M}:G_{g,D}P_{f,D}M\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{f',D}G_{g',D}M$$
be exactly the specified proper direct-image mate followed by the canonical open comparison of [lem-pur-weil-semilinear-exchange-reindexing]. For $C_T=-\otimes^L_{R_{E,T}}R_{F,T}$ write $c_{f,M}:C_YP_{f,E}M\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{f,F}C_XM$, and similarly $c_{f'}$, for [lem-pur-compact-support-integral-coefficient-comparison], using its canonical identification with strict-tower scalar extension. Let $J_u:C_{\mathrm{source}(u)}G_{u,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{u,F}C_{\mathrm{target}(u)}$ be the normalized pullback/scalar comparison [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension, lem-pur-normalized-scalar-comparison-realization]. On the stated domains these actual transformations satisfy
$$P_{f',F}(J_{g',M})\,c_{f',G_{g',E}M}\,C_{Y'}(\xi_{E,M})
=\xi_{F,C_XM}\,G_{g,F}(c_{f,M})\,J_{g,P_{f,E}M}.$$

This equation also holds in the ordinary derived categories of entire strict coefficient systems before total derived inverse limit [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Specifically put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $B_n=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_F=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^{hn}$ for $n\ge1$, and use scalar extension $C_T^{(n)}=-\otimes^L_{(A_n)_T}(B_n)_T$ on the actual reduction systems. In the displayed equation replace each integral operation and comparison by its simultaneous finite-system construction: $c$ is the ordered proper coefficient tensor map followed by the open coefficient identification, $J$ is balanced scalar association, and $\xi$ is the proper mate followed by the unit-normalized open exchange. These are the strict-system constructions specified in [lem-pur-compact-support-integral-coefficient-comparison, lem-pur-weil-semilinear-exchange-reindexing], restricted on the $F$ side to the actual indices $hn$. Their two composites are equal as derived-system maps, with all quotient transitions. Under the specified cofinal reduction/limit comparisons their total limits are precisely the integral maps in the displayed equation. The assertion is natural in $M$ and independent of compactification under the canonical refinement comparisons. It involves neither a purity map nor an exceptional inverse image nor a Weil datum.

proof.text: Finite coefficient coherence is proEtaleCoefficientInverseImageMap_comp [lem-pur-proetale-constant-ring-composition] applied to the finite quotient ring, followed by Iso.ext. The coefficient comparison is exactly sfConstantCoefficientIso, so this proves finiteCoherent without any exchange or scalar assertion.

Work first in the ordinary derived categories of strict $A_\bullet$- and $B_\bullet$-systems. Choose one $\mathcal O_E$-basis of $\mathcal O_F$ by [lem-sfb-local-field-integral-basis]. Reducing this basis modulo $\varpi_E^n$ gives compatible bases of $B_n/A_n$: the transition sends each reduced basis vector to itself at the smaller index. In particular this is the finite-free situation, with the actual $F$-indices $hn$, of [lem-coef-finite-free-system-restriction]. Write $T_W\dashv U_W$ for its derived scalar-extension/restriction adjunction and $\eta_N:N\to U_WT_WN$ for its unit, induced by $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Write $\mathscr P_{f,C}=Rp_{*,C}j_{!,C}$ and $G_{u,C}=u^{-1}_\bullet$ for $C=A,B$. The system operations, adjunctions and mate words exist before evaluation by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Throughout the calculation insert the canonical restriction/geometry comparisons, so that $UG_B=G_AU$ and $U\mathscr P_B=\mathscr P_AU$. The actual reduction system $M_\bullet$ is normalized by tensor reassociation; its levels are bounded constructible with finite Tor amplitude by the assumed integral domain. Thus it is an allowed input for the system scalar comparisons below.

proof.text: Let $x_C:G_{g,C}\mathscr P_{f,C}\to\mathscr P_{f',C}G_{g',C}$ be the specified system exchange. Its proper factor is the direct-image mate of the inverse-image square and its open factor is the inverse of the open-unit transpose, exactly as in [lem-pur-weil-semilinear-exchange-reindexing]. The simultaneous adjunction words are maps on entire derived systems by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Under the restriction comparisons, [lem-coef-finite-free-system-restriction] preserves the geometric units, counits and compositors. Substituting those comparisons into the proper unit--square--counit word therefore gives the $A$-word. For the open factor the restrictions of the two transposes agree, since both are the open unit with the same inverse-image compositor; the adjunction bijection gives agreement of the open factors and hence of their inverses. Composing the two factors gives $U_{Y'}(x_{B,N})=x_{A,U_XN}$ for every system input $N$ under these canonical identifications. This is equality of the specified system words, not a conclusion from their evaluated components.

source.place: Constituent coefficient-compatibility assembly paragraph; agent expansion, scalar-adjunction argument, Step 2.

proof.text:
Write $a_{f,N}:T_Y\mathscr P_{f,A}N\to\mathscr P_{f,B}T_XN$ for the ordered proper tensor comparison followed by open balancing. By [lem-coef-system-scalar-projection-identification] this actual ordered map is the scalar-adjunction mate of $\mathscr P_{f,A}U\cong U\mathscr P_{f,B}$, including refinement normalization. Consequently its adjunct is
$$U_Y(a_{f,N})\eta_{\mathscr P_{f,A}N}=\mathscr P_{f,A}(\eta_N),$$
and the same holds for $f'$. Let $b_{u,N}:T_{\mathrm{source}(u)}G_{u,A}N\to G_{u,B}T_{\mathrm{target}(u)}N$ be balanced scalar association. Its adjunct is
$$U(b_{u,N})\eta_{G_{u,A}N}=G_{u,A}(\eta_N).$$
Indeed the scalar unit of [lem-coef-finite-free-system-restriction] inserts $1$, and balanced association takes $u^{-1}x\otimes1$ to $u^{-1}(x\otimes1)$. This identity holds termwise on simultaneous tensor representatives, commutes with every quotient transition, and localizes to the system adjunction. Thus the formulas use the normalized $a,b$, rather than arbitrary isomorphisms between their endpoints.

proof.text: Apply total derived limit to Step 4. The limit is a functor on the derived system category by [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], so it preserves this equality. The strict-tower presentations of [lem-pur-compact-support-integral-coefficient-comparison] identify $a_f,a_{f'}$ with the specified integral $c_f,c_{f'}$. The specified exchange and its actual strict lift are the ordered reindexing maps by [lem-pur-weil-semilinear-exchange-reindexing]. For $b_u$, [lem-pur-normalized-scalar-comparison-realization] identifies the integral pullback/scalar map with the total limit of balanced association on simultaneous quotient representatives. This also gives the same map on our cofinal presentation: at $m=hn$, its tensor presentation first uses $A_{E,hn}\to A_{F,hn}$; passing instead through $A_{E,n}\to A_{F,hn}$ collapses both tensors to $P\otimes A_{F,hn}$ by $(x\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes ab$. Both routes commute with the quotient transitions and send $u^{-1}x\otimes b$ to $u^{-1}(x\otimes b)$. Hence they induce the identical balanced system comparison under these reassociations. Finally [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] identifies ordinary completed-ring tensor with strict-tower scalar extension by the actual quotient-augmentation map. These are the specified cofinal reduction/limit identifications in the question. The total-limit images of $L,R$ are therefore precisely its two integral composites, and their equality is the required integral equation.

proof.text: For the integral input-morphism naturality clause, the left path has three factors: scalar extension of the exchange component, the scalar compact-support comparison, and compact support of the balanced scalar-pullback component. Apply naturality to each factor, map the corresponding squares under the outer functors, and paste the three squares using associativity. For the right path, compose the whiskered scalar-pullback, coefficient comparison and exchange natural transformations, inserting the canonical functor associators; the associators have identity components, so this is the specified right path. Its naturality gives the other equation. Membership in the two-element set selects these two cases. This proves rectangle_naturality without assuming equality of the paths. Every construction and the adjunct computation is likewise natural in the input system. For a change of compactification insert the canonical refinement comparisons on all four compact-support terms. The scalar/refinement square of [lem-coef-system-scalar-projection-identification] identifies the two choices of $a_f,a_{f'}$ on systems. The refinement compatibility of the specified reindexing exchange in [lem-pur-weil-semilinear-exchange-reindexing] identifies the two choices of $x_A,x_B$. Thus conjugating the equality of Step 4 by these comparisons gives the equality for the other compactification: the intermediate comparison and its inverse cancel, while naturality moves the remaining ones to the endpoints. Comparisons through a common refinement have the same result by the cocycle asserted in the system scalar lemma. On integral objects the $c$ comparisons are independent of compactification by [lem-pur-compact-support-integral-coefficient-comparison], and the specified exchange has the same refinement normalization. Taking the limits as in Step 5 therefore gives the asserted independence for the integral equation as well. The calculation only uses underlying-scheme isomorphisms; it never requires $k$-linearity of $g$ or $g'$.

proof.text: For integralScalarIsomorphismExchange_integral, obtain a positive ramification exponent from the valuation-ring DVR description: the nonzero, nonunit image of the source uniformizer is a unit times a positive power of the target uniformizer. Map the principal source ideal to obtain Ramification. Apply strictLimitEquation_of_integralScalarIsomorphismExchange at this exponent. Its final clause identifies the two integral paths after the same target presentation, completion unit and cofinal Roos map. The presentation is an isomorphism, the completion unit is asserted invertible, and the cofinal chain map is a quasi-isomorphism, so its derived image is invertible. Evaluate the clause at each member of its two-element set, equate the resulting composites, and cancel the common invertible target composite. This proves the integral equality without a separate coefficient-exchange argument.

The completed integral equality is the previously isolated integral clause, while the simultaneous finite-level equality and the normalized total-limit clause are supplied by the two strictly smaller statements finiteScalarIsomorphismExchange and strictLimitEquation_of_integralScalarIsomorphismExchange. Combining these three clauses gives the displayed conjunction.
